artifacts.summary: All 4 plan phases complete: post-add index-state verification in git-commit-scoped.sh (V7), six new regression cases plus a negative control, a new git-staging-scope.md subsection, and a full-gate close-out with every failure attributed.

completion_data.completion_summary: Replaced git-commit-scoped.sh's blind git-add exit-code guard with post-add index-state verification so a tracked, ignore-matched positive pathspec's advisory false negative no longer aborts the whole commit, while a genuine add failure still refuses with exit 2. Added 6 regression cases plus a negative control (test-git-commit-scoped.sh: 32 passed, 0 failed) and a new git-staging-scope.md subsection documenting the hazard and the check-ignore -q prohibition. Full verify-deploy.sh gate run: FAIL 3 of 34, all attributable to this task's own un-redeployed source-store edits (gates 3/5) or to other concurrently-dispatched tasks (gate 8); none caused by this task's logic.

memory_candidates.content: When a git-add positive pathspec names a TRACKED file whose path matches a .gitignore rule via a parent-directory pattern, `git add` prints the ignore advisory and exits 1, but still stages the file correctly (verified git 2.54.0). `git check-ignore -q` cannot detect this: it is index-aware and reports 'not ignored' for exactly these tracked paths, contradicting git add. The only reliable fix is post-add verification of actual index state (git ls-files --error-unmatch + git diff --quiet), never trusting git add's exit code in either direction -- this also avoids papering over a genuine add failure (e.g. an out-of-repo pathspec, which hard-fails with nothing staged).
